ee6ddc5dae67d840.heading: Charitable giving tax relief (Self Assessment helpsheet HS342)

amounts.name: Payroll Giving relief cap
amounts.value: greater of £50,000 or 25% of adjusted total income

caveats: Charities based in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Norway can no longer apply for tax relief; relief obtained on or before 14 March 2023 continued only until April 2024.
No reliefs will be given on gifts to non-UK charities after 5 April 2024.

Guidance instructs users to check the online 'Tax relief when you donate to a charity' guide or a tax adviser before completing boxes 5-10, as reliefs may change and not be reflected in this helpsheet.
If using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, claims/adjustments are made through compatible software instead of the Self Assessment boxes referenced.
HMRC cannot accept a first claim or higher claim for Gift Aid carry-back in an amended tax return for the year ended 5 April 2026 - must be in the original return.
No additional relief is due for basic rate taxpayers unless claiming certain allowances for people aged over 65.

deadlines.name: Gift Aid carry-back to previous tax year
deadlines.rule: payments made between 6 April 2026 and date of submitting return for year ended 5 April 2026 can be carried back; must be claimed in original return, before appropriate filing date

definitions.meaning: A scheme providing relief for gifts of money to UK based charities that meet the UK tax definition of a charity, treated as made after deduction of basic rate Income Tax.
Community Amateur Sports Club registered with HMRC as such when a Gift Aid donation is made; broadly same Gift Aid rules as charities but cannot claim Gift Aid on membership subscriptions.

Shares/securities listed on a recognised stock exchange, dealt on AIM or PLUS-Quoted Market, units in an Authorised Unit Trust, shares in an OEIC, or interests in certain overseas collective investment schemes.
Liabilities to which the charity becomes subject in connection with the transfer of shares/securities or property, deducted when calculating relief.
The whole of a person's beneficial interest in freehold or leasehold land in the UK.

obligations.must: have paid enough Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax to cover tax reclaimed by charity/CASC, or pay an additional amount of Income Tax if not
obligations.trigger: making Gift Aid donations exceeding tax paid
obligations.who: Self Assessment taxpayer donating via Gift Aid

obligations.must: enter total Gift Aid payments in boxes 5, 6, 7 and 8 on page TR 4

obligations.deadline: before the appropriate filing date, in original return for year ended 5 April 2026
obligations.must: make the claim in their original tax return for the year ended 5 April 2026 (not an amended return)
obligations.trigger: wanting relief on donations made between 6 April 2026 and date of filing to be given for the earlier year
obligations.who: Self Assessment taxpayer wanting to carry back Gift Aid relief

obligations.must: enter relief claimed for gifts of shares/securities in box 9 on page TR 4
obligations.trigger: making qualifying gift/sale of shares or securities to charity

obligations.must: enter relief claimed for gifts of land/buildings in box 10 on page TR 4
obligations.trigger: making qualifying gift/sale of property to charity

obligations.must: report Payroll Giving donations on the Additional Information pages; not enter donations elsewhere on the return
obligations.trigger: participating in a Payroll Giving scheme
obligations.who: Self Assessment taxpayer using Payroll Giving

obligations.must: keep records/documents relating to the gifts (Gift Aid amounts, share/property transfer documents) in case HMRC asks for more information
obligations.who: Self Assessment taxpayer claiming these reliefs

note.summary: HS342 explains four tax reliefs for charitable giving to be reported on the Self Assessment tax return: Gift Aid, gifts of shares/securities, gifts of land/buildings, and Payroll Giving. It details how relief is calculated (including grossing-up for higher/additional rate taxpayers), which tax return boxes (5-10 on TR4) to use, the carry-back rule for Gift Aid payments, and the cap on Payroll Giving relief. It also notes changes affecting relief on gifts to non-UK charities and record-keeping requirements.
